findings.title: Double-checked locking is incomplete; concurrent callers may redundantly re-read the manifest
findings.body: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache`. If multiple goroutines call GetWebAssets concurrently before the cache is populated (e.g., during startup in non-dev mode), each will serialize on the write lock and redundantly read assets-manifest.json from disk and re-decode it. The proper double-checked locking pattern requires a second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock (gated on `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`, since dev mode intentionally bypasses the cache), so that only the first caller does the I/O and subsequent callers return the cached value. As written, every concurrent caller that arrives between the RUnlock at line 43 and the Lock at line 48 pays the full disk-read cost.

findings.title: No test exercises the concurrent path; the race fix is not regression-protected
findings.body: The PR adds synchronization to fix a data race on the global `entryPointAssetsCache`, but no test file is added or modified (the changed-files list contains only `pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go`). Without a concurrent test run under `go test -race` that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, future refactors could easily reintroduce the race — for example by reverting to a bare read of the global, by moving the `defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()` above the assignment on line 70, or by replacing the RWMutex with a non-sync primitive. A test that spawns N goroutines all calling GetWebAssets and waits on a sync.WaitGroup would have caught the original race and will catch any regression.
